pairs.question: Quinam te, qui casus, dux maxime, fessae eripuit patriae, cum talis horrida poscant bella uiros?
pairs.answer: Fesso mihi proxima tandem lux gratos Phaethontis equos auertit et atris aeternum demisit aquis.
pairs.derivation: Scipio addresses the shade of Appius Claudius. Dropped the speech tag 'ait' (its embedded vocative 'dux maxime' is kept, contiguous span preserved). Quoted only the interrogative sentence; the following lines ('nec enim dextra concesserit ulli Appius aut astu...') are praise/narration not needed for sense, so omitted. Answer ('Contra quae ductor:' framing dropped) is the reply's first full sentence, ending at 'aquis.' = he died (the last dawn sank its horses in dark waters forever); the rest of his speech turns to asking Scipio's help with his burial. Stripped inline verse numbers 450, 460.

pairs.question: O magni mihi numinis instar, cara parens, quam, te ut nobis uidisse liceret, optassem Stygias uel leto intrare tenebras! quae sors nostra fuit, cui te, cum prima subiret, eripuit sine honore dies et funere carpsit?
pairs.answer: Nullos, o nate, labores mors habuit nostra: aetherio dum pondere partum exsoluor, miti dextra Cyllenia proles imperio Iouis Elysias deduxit in oras attribuitque paris sedes, ubi magna moratur Alcidae genetrix, ubi sacro munere Leda.
pairs.derivation: Scipio asks his dead mother Pomponia how/by what fate she was taken. Dropped 'sic iuuenis prior:' tag; quoted the whole contiguous speech (the opening wish supplies context for the closing interrogative). Answer ('excipit his mater:' framing dropped) is her first full sentence, ending at 'Leda.' (the colon after 'nostra' is not a sentence end): her death was painless, Mercury led her to Elysium. The rest ('uerum age, nate, tuos ortus...') turns to a new topic, Scipio's divine origin. Stripped inline verse numbers 625, 630, 635.

pairs.question: Quot milia toto credis in orbe, puer, lustras dum singula uisu, descendisse Erebo?
pairs.answer: nullo non tempore abundans umbrarum huc agitur torrens, uectatque capaci agmina mole Charon, et sufficit improba puppis.
pairs.derivation: The Sibyl poses a rhetorical question to Scipio and answers it herself. Dropped the narrative framing 'ni magna sacerdos admoneat turbae innumerae:'. Question and self-given answer are contiguous; answer runs to the end of the utterance ('puppis.'). Stripped inline verse number 760.

pairs.question: Libyci certissima proles Hammonis, quando exuperat tua gloria cunctos indubitata duces similique cupidine rerum pectora nostra calent, quae te uia, fare, superbum ad decus et summas laudum perduxerit arces.
pairs.answer: Turpis lenti sollertia Martis. audendo bella expedias.
pairs.derivation: Scipio asks Alexander's shade by what road he reached his glory. Dropped 'incipit Aeneades:' tag; quoted the whole address (which builds to the indirect question 'quae te uia... perduxerit arces'). Answer ('ille sub haec:' framing dropped): the operative answering sentences = boldness, not the slow craft of war, wins ('by daring you accomplish wars'); stopped before the digression 'pigra extulit artis...'. Stripped inline verse number 770.

pairs.question: Dic, hic quinam, uirgo? nam luce refulget praecipua frons sacra uiro, multaeque secuntur mirantes animae et laeto clamore frequentant. qui uultus! quam, si Stygia non esset in umbra, dixissem facile esse deum!
pairs.answer: Non falleris: meruit deus esse uideri, et fuit in tanto non paruum pectore numen.
pairs.derivation: Scipio asks the Sibyl who the radiant shade (Homer) is. Dropped the 'ait' tag. Answer ('inquit docta comes Triuiae' framing dropped) is her first full sentence, ending at 'numen.', directly answering Scipio's 'esse deum' ('You are not wrong: he deserved to seem a god'); the further identification ('carmine complexus terram...') is elaboration, omitted. Stripped inline verse numbers 780, 785.

pairs.question: Restare haec ordine duro lamentor rebus Latiis. sed luce remota si nulla est uenia et merito mors ipsa laborat, perfidiae Poenus quibus aut Phlegethontis in undis exuret ductor scelus, aut quae digna renatos ales in aeternum laniabit morsibus artus?
pairs.answer: Ne metue: non uita sequetur inuiolata uirum: patria non ossa quiescent.
pairs.derivation: Scipio asks the Sibyl with what punishment the Carthaginian leader (Hannibal) will expiate his treachery. Dropped 'Tum iuuenis lacrimans:' tag; kept the contiguous speech (the lament supplies the 'luce remota si nulla est uenia' setup for the interrogative). Answer ('exclamat uates' framing dropped) is the first full sentence, ending at 'quiescent.': his life will not go unharmed, his bones will not rest; the following lines narrate the detail of his exile and death. Stripped inline verse numbers 870, 875.
